fact: Fingernails grow about 3 mm a month. Toenails are much slower.
nfact: Evonne Goolagong Cawley, a Wiradjuri woman, won seven Grand Slam singles titles.

fact: Dr Dinesh Palipana was injured in a car crash as a medical student, went back, graduated, and became Queensland’s first quadriplegic medical intern.
nfact: Botanically, bananas are berries. Strawberries are not.

fact: Gertrude Elion shared the 1988 Nobel Prize in Medicine. Her drugs include allopurinol, azathioprine and aciclovir, and she never finished a PhD.
nfact: Dame Whina Cooper led the 1975 Māori Land March to Wellington at the age of 79.

fact: The stapes in the middle ear is the smallest bone in the body, about 3 mm long.
nfact: Kiwifruit used to be sold as ‘Chinese gooseberries’ until New Zealand growers renamed them in 1959.

fact: The thyroid is a butterfly-shaped gland at the front of the neck. Its hormones help set how fast the body uses energy.
nfact: The Mpemba effect, where hot water sometimes freezes faster than cold, is named after Tanzanian student Erasto Mpemba.

fact: Melatonin, sometimes called the hormone of darkness, is made by the pineal gland, mostly at night.
nfact: Butterflies taste with their feet.

fact: Françoise Barré-Sinoussi co-discovered HIV in 1983 and shared the 2008 Nobel Prize in Medicine.
nfact: Watermelon is about 92% water.

fact: PCOS is one of the most common hormone conditions, affecting roughly 8 to 13% of women of reproductive age.
nfact: Actor Hedy Lamarr co-invented a frequency-hopping system in 1942, an idea later echoed in Wi-Fi and Bluetooth.

fact: A pill’s coating isn’t just for taste: enteric coatings protect some medicines from stomach acid, or the stomach from the medicine.
nfact: A group of owls is called a parliament.

fact: Insulin was first given to a patient, 14-year-old Leonard Thompson, in Toronto in January 1922.
nfact: Ada Lovelace published what is often called the first computer program, in 1843.

fact: Stretched out, the DNA in a single human cell would be about 2 metres long.
nfact: A pineapple plant takes around two years to grow a single pineapple.

fact: The Royal Flying Doctor Service made its first flight in 1928.
nfact: Valentina Tereshkova became the first woman in space in 1963.

fact: Associate Professor Kelvin Kong, a Worimi man, became Australia’s first Aboriginal surgeon.
nfact: Katherine Johnson checked the orbit calculations for John Glenn’s 1962 flight. He asked for her by name.

fact: The cornea has no blood vessels. It gets most of its oxygen straight from the air.
nfact: Lightning is about five times hotter than the surface of the Sun.

fact: Dr Charles Drew, an African American surgeon, pioneered large-scale blood banking and plasma storage in the 1940s.
nfact: Cathy Freeman lit the cauldron at the Sydney 2000 Olympics, then won 400 m gold ten days later.

fact: Insulin was discovered in Toronto in 1921 by Frederick Banting and Charles Best, with James Collip and John Macleod.
nfact: Sharks are older than trees, by tens of millions of years.

fact: Rosalyn Yalow co-developed radioimmunoassay, letting labs measure tiny amounts of hormones like insulin. She won the 1977 Nobel Prize in Medicine.
nfact: A day on Venus is longer than its year.

fact: A red blood cell lives about 120 days and laps your circulation many thousands of times.
nfact: Scotland’s national animal is the unicorn.

fact: The brain is about 2% of body weight but uses around 20% of the body’s energy at rest.
nfact: Apples float because roughly a quarter of their volume is air.

fact: Lady Mary Wortley Montagu promoted smallpox inoculation in Britain in 1721, decades before Jenner’s cowpox vaccine.
nfact: Wilma Rudolph wore a leg brace as a child after polio, then won three sprint golds at the 1960 Olympics.

fact: Skin is the body’s largest organ.
nfact: Paralympian Kurt Fearnley crawled the 96 km Kokoda Track in 2009.

fact: Your heart beats roughly 100,000 times a day.
nfact: Bubble wrap was first invented in 1957 as a textured wallpaper.

fact: The first X-ray of a human body part, in 1895, was of Anna Bertha Röntgen’s hand, wedding ring and all.
nfact: Neville Bonner became the first Aboriginal member of Australia’s federal parliament in 1971.

fact: The average age of menopause in Australia is around 51.
nfact: Mary Anning helped uncover one of the first ichthyosaur fossils in 1811, when she was about 12.

fact: Elizabeth Blackwell became the first woman to earn a medical degree in the United States, in 1849.
nfact: Owls can’t move their eyes, so they turn their heads, up to about 270 degrees.

fact: Research by Professor Fiona Stanley and Dr Carol Bower helped show that folate before pregnancy prevents neural tube defects such as spina bifida.
nfact: Ash Barty, a Ngarigo woman, won Wimbledon in 2021.

fact: The word ‘hormone’ was coined in 1905 by physiologist Ernest Starling, from the Greek for ‘to set in motion’.
nfact: The dot over a lowercase i or j is called a tittle.

fact: The medical name for hiccups is singultus.
nfact: The shortest war on record, between Britain and Zanzibar in 1896, lasted under an hour.

fact: Mary Seacole, a Jamaican-born nurse, ran the ‘British Hotel’ near Balaclava, feeding and nursing soldiers in the Crimean War.
nfact: The ‘seeds’ on a strawberry are actually tiny fruits, each with a seed inside.

fact: Florence Nightingale used a ‘rose diagram’ to show that most Crimean War soldiers died of preventable disease, not wounds.
nfact: Flamingos are pink because of pigments in the algae and shrimp they eat.

fact: Heart attack symptoms in women can include breathlessness, nausea, and jaw, neck or back pain, not just chest pain.
nfact: Earth’s days are getting very slightly longer over time, as the Moon’s tides slow its spin.
